newsitem.title: UK: Agreement reached at Ford's English plant.
newsitem.headline: Agreement reached at Ford's English plant.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. and union leaders said they reached an agreement Friday over the future of a British plant, averting the threat of national strikes.
Ford last month announced plans to move production of its new Escort model from its Halewood, Merseyside plant in northern England to continental Europe.

The agreement came after two days of talks between Ford's European head, Jac Nasser, and leaders of the Transport and General Workers Union and the Amalgamated Engineers and Electricians Unions in a last-ditch effort by the workers to save 1,300 jobs at the plant.

Unions said that under the deal, there would be fewer than the 1,300 job losses originally planned at Halewood. Production of the Escort would still move to Germany and Spain, but union leaders said mainstream models would continue to be made at Halewood.
A strike ballot of all Ford workers in Britain has been called off and the deal is expected to be put to a meeting of Halewood workers next week.
